explanation: Tipping (bahşiş) is discretionary in Turkey but widely practiced to reward good service, with about 10% being typical at restaurants (more at upscale places). Some restaurants already add a service charge, in which case extra tipping isn't required, and cash is preferred since card tips don't always reach staff.
local_tip: Leave around 10% in cash on the table or hand it to the server directly, and check the bill first for an already-included service charge.
regional_note: Tipping is lighter and more informal (rounding up the bill) outside tourist areas, while in hubs like Istanbul and Antalya closer to 10-15% is expected.

also_check.note: Tipping is considered insulting as it implies the staff needs extra money; excellent service is the standard.
Tipping 15-20% is expected for service staff, as wages are often below minimum.
A service charge is included by law, but leaving small change is polite; overtipping can seem showy.
